subject: Shared home-office layouts
hook: One worktop, two workstations — here's how it's built.
ig:
One worktop, two workstations — here's how a shared desk comes together in the workshop.

A long desk for two is cut as one piece where the wall allows, so there's no join running between you. Then:

— the exposed front edge goes through the edge bander for a sealed ABS finish
— the boring machine drills each pedestal for drawer runners and shelf pins
— two pedestals are assembled, one per person
— cable grommets go in at both seats so each workstation has its own route to power

Everything is made in our own Hanley workshop and checked before it leaves. On site, we fit the desk to the wall, not the other way round.

Working from home with someone else? Comment DESK and we'll send you the link to our home office desk page.
fb:
Ever wondered how a fitted desk for two actually gets made?

This reel follows the process in our Hanley workshop: the worktop cut on the panel saw, edges sealed on the edge bander, pedestals drilled for drawers on the boring machine, then assembled and fitted with a cable grommet at each seat.

It's built to the width of your wall, so two people get proper workstations without fighting over the last few centimetres. Have a look at our home office desk page if you're planning one.
